title: Routing and ARP
intro: Before a packet can reach a service, the host has to decide which interface and which next hop to send it through. When that decision is wrong, nothing above it matters.

steps.prompt: Ask the kernel exactly which route it would use to reach 10.20.0.15.
steps.explanation: Traffic to 10.20.0.15 leaves through eth0, via gateway 10.0.4.1, with source address 10.0.4.15.
steps.why: Reading the whole routing table and working out which rule matches is error-prone. 'ip route get' asks the kernel directly for its actual decision — including which source IP it will use, which matters for firewall rules on the other end.

steps.prompt: Show the routing table in numeric form (the older command, still common in docs and scripts).
steps.explanation: Same information as 'ip route', older format. 0.0.0.0 destination = the default route.
steps.why: Recognize both formats — 'route' and 'ifconfig' are deprecated but appear everywhere in older runbooks and still exist on many systems. -n skips slow reverse DNS lookups for each address.

steps.prompt: Show the ARP table: which MAC addresses this host has learned for IPs on its local network.
steps.fake_output:
? (10.0.4.1) at 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f [ether] on eth0
? (10.0.4.30) at <incomplete> on eth0
steps.explanation: The gateway resolved fine; 10.0.4.30 is <incomplete> — this host tried to reach it and got no ARP reply at all.
steps.why: An <incomplete> entry for a same-subnet host means the problem is at layer 2: the other machine is down, on a different VLAN, or has the wrong IP configured. No firewall rule can explain it, because traffic never got that far.

steps.prompt: Add a temporary static route sending 192.168.50.0/24 through a VPN gateway at 10.0.4.254.
steps.explanation: Traffic for that subnet now goes to the VPN gateway instead of the default route.
steps.why: Routes added with 'ip route add' vanish on reboot — fine for testing, but a production route must be persisted in the OS's network config (netplan, NetworkManager) or, in the cloud, in the VPC route table instead.
